newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds advance on U.S. inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds advance on U.S. inflation data.

text.p: 1630 GMT - The Austrian bond market regained ground from early losses on Wednesday, boosted by the release of lower-than-expected U.S. inflation data, and traders predicted further gains on the back of U.S. strength.
"Interest rate fears have died down again somewhat," said one trader, referring to a drop in U.S. April producer prices which point to lower chances of a U.S. rate hike.
The U.S. market and German Bund future rose on the data.
"Naturally we hopped on the back of their gains," another trader said.
* 10 year benchmark 5.75 pct bond maturing July 2006 down five bps at 100.40 to yield 5.69 (5.69) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.57/65 to yield 5.67/66.
* Latest five-year 4.375 bond maturing February 2002 closed unchanged at 98.95 in bourse trade to yield 4.58 (4.58) pct, quoted post-market at 99.05/15 to yield 4.56/54 percent.
* Austrian bond future up 20 bps at 109.52 on turnover of 219 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany down one bp at minus one, five-year spread up one bp at ten.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.437 and overnight money just lower at 3.10/3.35. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
